question: Which Linux companion app direction, if any, should OpenClaw core sponsor for this issue now that Windows Hub is shipped?
rationale: The remaining work is a large native desktop surface with competing implementation tracks and security-sensitive gateway, auth, pairing, and command-execution boundaries, so automation should not choose the product architecture.

options.title: Choose one native GTK track
options.body: Select either the C/GTK or Rust/GTK PR as the canonical path and require security, packaging, upgrade, and real desktop proof before merge.

options.title: Split into narrower Linux milestones
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella but move notifications, tray, pairing, packaging, and diagnostics into separate reviewed milestones.

options.title: Defer core Linux companion
options.body: Leave Linux users on Gateway, CLI, and Control UI for now and keep companion efforts external until maintainer capacity and security posture are clearer.

recommendation.title: Choose one native GTK track
recommendation.body: Select either the C/GTK or Rust/GTK PR as the canonical path and require security, packaging, upgrade, and real desktop proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion contains steipete's product-direction comments for a GTK-native Linux app and the current priority tradeoff.
